doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 17 august — «Sfântul Mucenic Tirs»

attestations.note: doxologia.ro prints «Sfântul Mucenic Tirs» twice: on 17 august, where the page behind the line opens neither a Viață nor a Tropar tab, and on 14 decembrie, where it prints the company's whole life — Thyrsus, Leucius, Callinicus, Philemon, Apollonius and Arianus (https://doxologia.ro/14-decembrie, read 25 September 2026). The row here is 17 august, which is the day the Russian calendar keeps and the day this folder was read from, and the December day is recorded here only. **Whether the two lines are one man is not settled**: the corpus's own rule is that two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, and the August line is too bare to test.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Αυγούστου — «Άγιοι Θύρσος, Λεύκιος, Κορωνάτος και η συνοδεία τους»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The Russian rows already keep the three on this menologion day and the Greek calendar keeps them on the revised-julian 17 August, under the same three names and with their company, «και η συνοδεία τους». The notice is two sentences and both are about the record rather than the passion. **The first is a hedge of the page's own: «Ίσως να συγχέονται με αυτούς της 14ης Δεκεμβρίου και το όνομα Καλλίνικος του τρίτου μάρτυρα να έγινε Κορωνάτος» — perhaps they are confused with those of 14 December, and the name Callinicus of the third martyr became Coronatus. The corpus keeps both a Coronatus and a `callinicus-of-caesarea` in this company, so the hedge is recorded here and in the reader's report and nothing is merged on it.** The second is the one positive thing: «Πάντως γι' αυτούς τους τρεις αναφέρεται ότι «τελείται αυτών η σύναξις πλησίον των Ελενιανών»» — of these three it is said that their synaxis is held near the Helenianai. The page gives no year and no emperor, so the folder's 249–251 from the Sretensky calendar stands. **A second and separate Coronatus stands on the Greek 13 Αυγούστου, «Άγιος Κορωνάτος», whose whole notice is that he was martyred by the sword; that is another day and another entry, and by the settled rule two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, so it is drafted as its own folder, `coronatus-13-august`, and the question is in the reader's report.** No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints a single distich for the three and no apolytikion and no kontakion, so no hymn is added.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 27.12.2025 (14. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Тирс, Левкије и Калиник.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, AN ENUMERATED THREE, so BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 counts three and each of the three folders takes this one heading whole with its closing full stop; the corpus holds all three and they are already `related` to one another. URL year 2025. He is the first name. **A DAY NO OTHER CALENDAR KEEPS HIM ON**: the Russian, Romanian and Greek rows on this folder are all 17 August, and this book puts him on the Julian 14 December with Leucius and Callinicus — which is the day the Romanian calendar keeps those two on and not him. The serbian row was `undocumented`, so the row lands here and none of the other three was touched. `types` UNTOUCHED: «мученици» is the `martyr` held. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the entry names the emperor «Кумврикије», Decius’s successor, and the «кесар Флавије» who built his church at the end of the fourth century, and gives neither of them a year; the 249–251 the folder carries is days.pravoslavie.ru’s and stands. `related_add`: `pulcheria-the-empress`, in both directions, on the entry’s closing sentence — «Светитељ се јавио у визији царици Пулхерији и препоручио јој, да сахрани мошти чердесет мученика до његових моштију», the saint appeared in a vision to the empress Pulcheria and advised her to bury the relics of the Forty Martyrs beside his own. A named apparition with an instruction in it is this folder’s story, on the reading made for `orestes-companion-of-eustratius` and `demetrius-of-rostov` on 12-13. NO ROW FOR THE FORTY MARTYRS: the corpus keeps them as forty separate folders and the entry names not one of them, so there is nobody to write a row to. NO OTHER `related` ROW: Leucius, Callinicus and `cornutus-of-iconium` are already here, and the bishop of Caesarea «Филеј» who baptised him is no folder this corpus holds. NO `locations`. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: that he and Leucius were honourable citizens of Caesarea in Bithynia, HE A CATECHUMEN AND NOT YET BAPTISED and Leucius already baptised; that it was the sight of Leucius’s death that kindled him; that an invisible hand of God healed his wounds, opened the prison doors and led him out, and that he went straight to the bishop to be baptised; that he bore his second torture as though in sleep and not awake, and that many idols fell at the power of his prayer; and that when they put him in a wooden chest to saw him through, the saw could not so much as scratch the wood, so that he rose out of the chest, gave thanks to God for his torments and gave up his spirit in peace. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Tirs, Levchie, Calinic, Filimon, Apolonie și Arian (a common of martyrs, printed once for the six together; «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own reading)

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received from you, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having your strength they overthrew the tormentors, and broke also the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.
